description_full: APi Group Corporation provides fire and life safety, security, elevator and escalator, and specialty services worldwide. It operates in two segments, Safety Services and Specialty Services. The company offers fire protection solutions; electronic security systems; and elevators and escalators, including the design, installation, inspection, service, and monitoring of life safety systems to high tech services, advanced manufacturing, healthcare, fulfillment and distribution centers, and critical infrastructure end markets. It also provides various specialty contracting, fabrication and distribution, and infrastructure and utility services to critical infrastructure, high tech services, and healthcare end markets. The company was formerly known as J2 Acquisition Limited and changed its name to APi Group Corporation in October 2019. APi Group Corporation was founded in 1926 and is headquartered in New Brighton, Minnesota.

financial_summary: APi Group Corporation is a large-cap industrials business with a $18.5B market cap on $7.9B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +6% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size. Operating margins are expanding by +2.3pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 6% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 27%.

The business throws off $663M in free cash flow — roughly 8 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.51× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.9× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 4.1×.
Shareholder yield is only 0.4%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 12% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

Free cash flow has compounded 7.7% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.07 (orders outpacing sales), a backlog worth 46% of annual revenue and deferred revenue up 18%.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (1.1x, 1.2% of sales), a maintenance pace.
